newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt picks airport sales advisers.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt picks airport sales advisers.

text.p: Australia on Thursday named its legal, business and accounting advisers for the second phase of its airport privatisation programme.
Finance Minister John Fahey said BZW had been chosen as business adviser, the Australian Government Solicitor as legal adviser and KPMG accounting adviser.

Expressions of interest for the sale of long-term leases for the 15 airports in phase two would be sought in September or October and the sales were expected to be finalised by June 30, 1998, Fahey said in a statement.
Sydney airports have been excluded from the second round of sales while the government determines where to build a second international airport for the country's largest city.

The 15 airports on offer in the second round include 10 major ports -- Adelaide, Alice Springs, Canberra, Coolangatta, Darwin, Hobart, Launceston, Townsville, Mount Isa and Tennant Creek, and five smaller airfields -- Archerfield, Essendon, Jandacot, Moorabbin and Parafield.
The government earlier this year sold long-term leases to Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth airports for a total A$3.3 billion, much higher than originally expected.
